audits.area: RELIABILITY & RESILIENCE: LLM Call Path, Worker Execution, Data Sync, Storage Hydration
audits.summary: ARGUS has strong foundational error handling (exponential backoff, circuit breaker, multi-fallback JSON parsing) but exhibits 8 critical failure modes in production: (1) streaming requests without explicit timeout guards can hang indefinitely when server sends no final chunk; (2) localStorage hydration silently degrades on schema mismatch/corruption without type validation or migration; (3) worker batch failure at Supabase sync layer leaves inconsistent local state with no user visibility; (4) fire-and-forget Supabase writes (observation-engine, hit-rate, mixed navigator promises) can fail silently after phase completion; (5) Promise.race with 30s fallback for validation callbacks lacks explicit state rollback if timeout fires; (6) AbortSignal on unmount does not guarantee in-flight Supabase/Analytics calls complete cleanup; (7) rate-limit quota display becomes stale when custom event dispatch misses edge cases; (8) merge logic at db.loadAndMerge can resurrect deleted items if remote/local timestamps conflict. Defens ive data access principle exists in CLAUDE.md but is NOT universally enforced in stores or worker prompts.

findings.title: Streaming requests without request timeout Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î infinite spinner on stuck server connection
findings.evidence: src/lib/llm.ts:627Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì757 (callLLMStream); no explicit timeout on reader.read() loop. src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1334 runs runDeepening without maxRetries config for the stream itself.
findings.impact: User sees 'Loading...' spinner forever if server enters zombie state (connected but not sending final chunk). No way to abort except page reload. Critical for slow networks or server degradation.
findings.fix_sketch: Add explicit AbortTimeout wrapper: wrap callLLMStream promise in Promise.race([stream, timeout(60000)]). On timeout, set error state with 'Request took too long' message and abort signal. Test with slow network throttling.

findings.title: localStorage hydration silent fails on corrupt/mismatched schema Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î app may crash or degrade silently
findings.evidence: src/lib/storage.ts:27Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì35 (getStorage) catches all JSON.parse errors and returns fallback. No validation that fallback shape matches expected interface. src/stores/useProgressiveStore.ts uses loaded data without validateShape check. Example: if stored ProgressiveSession lacks 'checkpoints' array, code at line 124 (progressAheadOfHead) will crash.
findings.impact: Old localStorage data from previous versions or corrupted state silently loads with missing fields. Optional chaining may mask the issue initially, but late property access (e.g., session.checkpoints[0].state_snapshot) throws ReferenceError and crashes the flow.
findings.fix_sketch: Add validateShape call in getStorage() fallback path with version/schema key. Create migration function in storage.ts that checks STORAGE_KEYS version and upgrades old shapes (e.g., add 'checkpoints': [] if missing). Log migration in development.

findings.title: Worker batch failure at Supabase upsert stage leaves inconsistent local state unvisible to user
findings.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1220Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì1228 (runAllAIWorkers + runPipeline via startWorkerExecution). Callbacks update UI (onComplete), but upsertToSupabase called inside db.ts is fire-and-forget. src/lib/db.ts:188Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì199 logs error to console, not user state. If Supabase sync fails, local worker.result is saved to localStorage but not persisted to DB; subsequent session reload may see stale data or lose work.
findings.impact: Worker completes with valid result, UI shows success, but Supabase upsert fails (e.g., network blip, quota). User thinks work is saved; on next device refresh, result is gone or out-of-sync.
findings.fix_sketch: Implement optimistic-then-persist pattern: onComplete callback sets UI state, but returns Promise that waits for Supabase confirmation. On error, show toast 'Saving...' then retry with exponential backoff (use withRetry from error-handler.ts). Add 'sync_status' field to worker to track ['pending_sync', 'synced', 'sync_failed'].

findings.title: Fire-and-forget Supabase writes in observation-engine and hit-rate silently fail after phase completion
findings.evidence: src/lib/observation-engine.ts:47 (runBatchAnalysis).catch(() => {}). src/lib/hit-rate.ts:69 similar pattern. src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1450,1561,1619 navigator/lead synthesis promises also .catch(() => {}).
findings.impact: Batch agent observations (used for personalization) silently fail if Supabase is down. Lead agent synthesis data not persisted. No indicator that learning loop broke. Next session, agent has no observations and behaves as if this session never happened.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace .catch(() => {}) with .catch(err => log.warn(...)) at minimum. Better: return result from onTaskApproved/onTaskRejected, let caller decide fire-and-forget vs. wait-for-sync. Add transaction log that records attempted writes so sync can retry on next startup.

findings.title: Promise.race with 30s timeout in worker validation lacks rollback on timeout Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î inconsistent state
findings.evidence: src/lib/worker-engine.ts:267Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì285. When validation fails, code calls onValidationFailed callback and races it against 30s timeout. If timeout fires, action='accept' is forced, but callback may have pending UI state (e.g., modal open waiting for user decision) that never resolves.
findings.impact: User sees validation modal, server times out after 30s, result is silently accepted without user input. User doesn't know the result was accepted; later feedback indicates confusion about the work.
findings.fix_sketch: On timeout, explicitly close UI modal state in callback wrapper. Return a callback result object with {action, timestamp} so caller can detect late resolutions and discard them. Add 'timed_out' action to handleValidation.

findings.title: AbortSignal on unmount does not guarantee cleanup of async Supabase calls Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î analytics/logs may not flush
findings.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:969Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì970 (cleanup on unmount). AbortController is set to null, but ongoing Supabase reads/writes in progress are not awaited. src/lib/db.ts loadAndMerge, syncToSupabase do not check signal.aborted.
findings.impact: User navigates away or refreshes while worker results are being synced. Partial Supabase transaction leaves orphaned records or inconsistent merge state. On next load, data may be duplicated or lost.
findings.fix_sketch: Add signal parameter to all Supabase functions (loadAndMerge, syncToSupabase, upsertToSupabase). Check signal.aborted in loops. Return early if aborted. Wrap unresolved Supabase promises in AbortController scope so they're managed, not orphaned.

findings.title: Rate-limit badge displays stale count when custom event 'argus:ratelimit' misses edge cases
findings.evidence: src/lib/llm.ts:722 dispatches 'argus:ratelimit' event in streaming only. If non-streaming callLLM is used, or if event listener is detached before dispatch, the component never updates. src/components/ui/RateLimitBadge.tsx:23Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì24 does not have error handler for event listener.
findings.impact: User sees stale 'Remaining: 10 / 50' but is actually at 2/50 (from non-stream calls). When they hit limit, they're surprised. Minor UX friction but misleading.
findings.fix_sketch: Dispatch rate-limit event from all callLLM paths (streaming and non-streaming). Add fallback: query current quota from /api/quota endpoint on mount and periodically. Use sessionStorage as cache so multiple tabs see same state.

findings.title: Merge logic at db.loadAndMerge resurrects deleted items on timestamp conflict Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î data integrity risk
findings.evidence: src/lib/db.ts:57Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì78 (mergeByTimestamp). Filters remote by !r.deleted_at but does not check local items for deleted_at flag. If local item has newer updated_at than remote (soft-deleted), it overwrites the remote deletion.
findings.impact: User deletes a project/persona on device A (soft-deleted locally with deleted_at timestamp). If device A is offline and then syncs before device B's deletion reaches server, the local-older deletion is lost. Deleted item resurfaces on next merge.
findings.fix_sketch: In mergeByTimestamp: if either local or remote has deleted_at, mark final result as deleted. Or: add deleted_at to the comparison: prefer the one with newer deleted_at timestamp, not updated_at. Test: create item, delete on device A (offline), sync device B deletion, verify item stays deleted.

findings.title: Defensive data access principle stated in CLAUDE.md but not enforced in worker prompts and AI_scope flows
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md Ïß†Defensive Data Access states 'LLM output may omit fields: result.classified_risks || []'. But src/lib/worker-engine.ts:76 directly accesses task.expected_output, task.persona, task.framework without fallbacks. src/lib/progressive-engine.ts:51Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤ì60 assumes LLM response has 'real_question', 'hidden_assumptions', 'skeleton' without optional chaining.
findings.impact: If LLM returns incomplete JSON (e.g., real_question is missing), worker flow crashes at parse stage instead of gracefully degrading. Test with a malformed LLM response that has missing fields.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap all LLM response field access in optional chaining or validateShape schema. Example: real_question = response.real_question || 'Unspecified question'. Run validation before using response in templates. Add test: LLM returns {hidden_assumptions: []} (missing real_question) Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î verify no crash.

top_3_priorities: URGENT (P0): Add explicit request timeout (60s) to callLLMStream with proper abort handling to prevent infinite spinners on stuck connections.
CRITICAL (P1): Implement localStorage migration & validation: validateShape on load, handle schema mismatch gracefully, version localStorage data to catch corruption.
HIGH (P1): Replace fire-and-forget Supabase writes with optimistic-then-persist pattern + sync status tracking. Make worker/observation/analytics persistence observable to user.

audits.summary: Argus has strong visual design and established information architecture but suffers from usability friction across navigation clarity, state feedback, mobile responsiveness, and accessibility. The 2670-line ProgressiveFlow component combines state orchestration with UI rendering, creating coupling that makes local changes risky. Error states are visible but don't guide users clearly. Mobile layout has calculated padding to work around fixed bars, but lacks true responsive redesign. Two parallel flows (progressive + legacy 4-step) create confusion without clear affordances to choose. Loading/skeleton states exist but are inconsistently applied. Keyboard navigation and focus management are nearly absent, and ARIA labels are minimal.

findings.title: ProgressiveFlow mega-component (2670 lines) couples state orchestration with UI rendering, making changes risky
findings.evidence: src/components/workspace/progressive/ProgressiveFlow.tsx:1-2670; 29 hooks, imports from worker-engine, llm, progressive-engine, three parallel data flows (questions, workers, drafts)
findings.impact: Users experience jank when a single hook dependency changes (e.g., adding a field to snapshot triggers 5+ re-renders). Developers hesitate to refactor for fear of breaking interactions. Changes to error handling or loading state ripple unpredictably.
findings.fix_sketch: Extract state orchestration (session lifecycle, phase transitions, worker coordination) into a pure reducer + custom hook (useProgressiveSession). ProgressiveFlow becomes a pure presenter consuming that hook. Move worker engine calls to separate effect hooks. Result: 1200-line flow component + 400-line session orchestrator.

findings.title: Mobile layout uses calculated padding (pb-[calc(120px+env...)]) to work around fixed bars instead of responsive redesign
findings.evidence: src/app/workspace/page.tsx:114 'pb-[calc(120px+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]'; logbook + worker drawers layer on mobile without true container queries or breakpoint-aware layout
findings.impact: On tablets (768px) or landscape phones, the bottom padding and hidden lg: components create dead space or content crush. Workers drawer occludes 56px fixed bar which occludes logbook drawer (56px) = 112px lost on small tablets. Long questions/answers wrap awkwardly. Users on small screens can't see agent sidebar at all.
findings.fix_sketch: Create mobile-first layout: (1) container query to ProgressiveFlow content width (max-content: 50rem on desktop); (2) responsive rail (hidden <lg, 320px on lg+, 360px xl+); (3) drawers use viewport-relative height not fixed px; (4) SafeArea hook for notch/home-indicator handling.

findings.title: Two parallel flows (progressive voyage vs legacy 4-step reframe/recast/rehearse) coexist without clear decision UI; users don't know which to choose
findings.evidence: src/app/workspace/page.tsx imports both ProgressiveFlow and ReframeStep/RecastStep/RehearseStep; /workspace routes to progressive by default, /tools/reframe/ to legacy; no onboarding or feature comparison.
findings.impact: New users land on workspace without understanding progressive is the new default. Existing users with reframe/recast projects see /project page navigation that jumps between systems. Handoff between flows (exportProgressiveAsReframe at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2253) is fragile. Features in one flow don't exist in the other (e.g., worker personas only in progressive).
findings.fix_sketch: Deprecate legacy flows or clearly separate: (1) dedicated landing page explaining 'Voyage (new)' vs 'Project Tools'; (2) project-level setting 'system: progressive | legacy'; (3) cross-system handoff validation + migration guide; (4) hide legacy UI once > 1 progressive project exists.
findings.depends_on: Phase 0: typed data pipeline (to make handoff robust)

findings.title: Error states appear but don't guide user recovery; rate-limit + login errors mixed with generic API failures
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2452-2471 renders errors in AnimatePresence but relies on error.includes('Ì≥≠Î∏≥Ì≥´Î£Ñ') substring matching; HeroFlow.tsx:247-258 has fragile login detection; no structured error codes or recovery actions for most failures
findings.impact: User gets 'Analysis failed' with no hint of next steps. Rate-limit error mentions 'Settings' but Settings lacks visible API key entry (need to know it's there). Worker failures map to 'waiting_input' status but UI doesn't clearly explain what input is needed or how to provide it.
findings.fix_sketch: Create ErrorResult type: {code: 'RATE_LIMIT' | 'AUTH_REQUIRED' | 'VALIDATION_ERROR' | 'WORKER_FAILURE', message, recoveryAction: {label, href, onClick}}. Render recoveryAction as clear button. Worker errors include field name + type hint.

findings.title: No keyboard navigation or focus management; accessibility beyond color contrast is minimal
findings.evidence: QuestionCard.tsx has onKeyDown for Enter in text inputs but no Tab between options; ProgressiveFlow modals (previewDraft, iterationOpen) have role='dialog' aria-modal=true but no focus trap or Escape key handler; 0 focus:ring styles on custom buttons
findings.impact: Screen reader users cannot navigate options. Keyboard-only users must use Tab excessively. Modal opens don't trap focus. Initial focus on question input is sometimes autoFocus, sometimes not (inconsistent). No visible focus indicator on gold accent buttons.
findings.fix_sketch: Use radix/ui Dialog for modals (built-in focus trap). QuestionCard: add tabIndex=0 to option buttons, useKeyDown hook for arrow keys. Global focus indicator: add focus:ring-2 ring-[var(--accent)] to all interactive elements. Test with keyboard-only nav.

findings.title: Loading/skeleton states exist (e.g., AnalysisCard skeleton) but are inconsistently applied; some phases show streaming text, others show nothing
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2200-2208 shows AnalysisCard with defaultCollapsed=true during conversing phase; skeleton array is populated but visual feedback is unclear; 'analyzing' phase shows streamingText in a separate block, not integrated into the question card
findings.impact: During first analysis or worker task, user sees nothing for 2-3 seconds, then content appears. No skeleton placeholder. During long LLM calls (e.g., dm_feedback), the UI feels frozen. Phase names ('Ì≥≠ÎπÜÌ≥≠Îπê ‰ª•Ì≤ÄÈçÆÌ≤Ñ', 'Ì≥≠ÎπÜÌ≥≠Îπê', 'ËπÇÎãøÌÄ¨') don't clearly map to user actions.
findings.fix_sketch: Create LoadingSkeleton component for each content type (question, analysis, feedback). Stream text incrementally into a pre-rendered skeleton with animated placeholder blocks. Add 'Analyzing your request...' + persona avatars as ambient feedback. Show phase progress bar at top (ProgressLine already exists, make it sticky).

findings.title: Scroll management is ad-hoc: scroll() and scrollToRef() called after effects, risk races and janky scroll-to-bottom on mobile
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2038-2042 scroll functions use window.scrollTo with 'smooth'; called in try-finally blocks but no cancellation token; 200/250ms timers mentioned in comment as problematic during user scrolling
findings.impact: If user scrolls while answer is being processed, scroll-to-bottom yanks viewport. On mobile with fixed bars and drawers, smooth scroll doesn't account for layout shift. New question card appears below fold because scroll happened before layout committed.
findings.fix_sketch: Use IntersectionObserver to scroll question into view only if out of viewport. Remove smooth scrolling to bottom (let user scroll). If critical content (error, new question) appears, use offset scroll + focus management instead.

findings.title: Response preview text (mix/draft) renders in <pre className=whitespace-pre-wrap> which can overflow on mobile; no word-wrap or truncation
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2554-2556 in draft preview modal renders final_text as pre; FinalCard likely does same; no max-width constraint on code blocks
findings.impact: Long output without spaces (URLs, UUIDs, or dense code) breaks mobile layout. User sees horizontal scroll. On narrow screens, pre-formatted text dominates and button/copy controls become unreachable.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap pre in div with max-w-full overflow-x-auto; add break-words class to inner text; provide 'Expand fullscreen' toggle for mobile reading.

findings.title: Branch/version history UI (VersionHistoryDrawer, versionLabel) exists but is buried; users don't know they can explore prior drafts or revert
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2319-2331 version chip is only shown in final state, positioned at end of page; no hint on main flow that branches are possible; draftIsOnBranch banner (line 2335) appears only when editing existing branch
findings.impact: User completes a draft, sees version history button for first time. No discoverability before that. If user wants to compare two branches, they must open modal from final state only. Cannot iterate on a mid-stream draft.
findings.fix_sketch: Add 'Version history' link in top nav (sticky bar) once 2+ drafts exist. Show branch count badge. Allow version history access from any phase (not just final). Preview should highlight 'Branch from here' as primary action.

findings.title: Persona pool selection (PersonaPoolModal) is a modal popup that appears only when deploying workers; no preview before adding
findings.evidence: WorkerPanel.tsx likely triggers PersonaPoolModal; persona selection happens in isolation from main flow; no way to 'preview what this persona will review before I commit'
findings.impact: User commits 3 personas to review without knowing if their concerns align with the plan. After review comes back, user realizes wrong persona was chosen and must restart. Context of what's being reviewed is lost in the modal.
findings.fix_sketch: Add 'Persona preview' card on main flow that shows who will review + their profile + what they'll focus on. Personas are selectable inline with drag-reorder. Link to pool search within preview, not in separate modal.

findings.title: Question/Answer history (AnsweredPills) is collapsed at bottom; users cannot revisit or edit earlier answers without scrolling deep
findings.evidence: ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2289-2292 AnsweredPills rendered at bottom in a collapsible detail block; referenced only by answeredPillsRef for 'Revisit my answers' link
findings.impact: User wants to double-check an early answer (e.g., success_criteria) but must scroll to bottom. If they edit, entire flow re-analyzes. No inline edit + re-run capability. Q&A context is lost in long scrolls.
findings.fix_sketch: Add collapsible 'Context' panel in right rail (or mobile drawer) showing Q&A breadcrumb. Each q/a pair has 'Edit & re-analyze' action that reruns just dependent phases. Sticky anchor to jump to any Q.
findings.depends_on: Phase 0: ContextChain (to track which phases depend on which answers)

findings.title: Decision maker (reviewer agent) selection UI is unclear; users don't understand why they need one or how to change it later
findings.evidence: ReviewerBadge at ProgressiveFlow.tsx:62-100 shows saved agent with emoji but no explanation; detected DM from initial analysis is auto-selected; no affordance to change it during voyage
findings.impact: Users don't realize a manager/reviewer is 'watching' their plan. If wrong DM is detected, it's too late. No 'Change reviewer' button during flow. Confusion about whether DM feedback is optional vs mandatory.
findings.fix_sketch: Add 'Your reviewer' card early in flow (after initial question) with 'Change' action. Show persona profile + what they focus on. Make it clear DM is optional ('or skip to dive deeper yourself'). Allow mid-flow changes to reset feedback.

findings.title: Three.js VoyageChart (branch visualization) is heavy and not optimized for mobile; renders in 2D but takes significant bundle + render time
findings.evidence: VoyageChart.tsx imports three.js and canvas elements; used in logbook to show version tree; no lazy loading or fallback 2D on mobile
findings.impact: Initial load includes three.js bundle (~200KB gzipped) even if user never opens the chart. On mobile, canvas rendering is slow and drains battery. Chart is visual-only (no accessibility tree).
findings.fix_sketch: Lazy load three.js only when VoyageChart modal opens. Provide 2D SVG fallback on mobile or devices with GPU constraints. Add prefers-reduced-motion:reduce to disable canvas animations.

findings.title: Form inputs (question text, revision directive) lack visual validation feedback; users don't know if input is too long, too short, or invalid until submit
findings.evidence: QuestionCard.tsx input has placeholder but no max-length hint or live validation; revision directive modal (ProgressiveFlow.tsx:2578-2699) has textarea with no character counter or dynamic height
findings.impact: User types a 10,000-char revision request, hits submit, backend rejects. Or very short input that seems too vague. No inline feedback to correct before wasting compute.
findings.fix_sketch: Add maxLength + remaining char counter on inputs > 100 chars. Textarea auto-expand + 1000-char soft limit. Real-time validation icon (checkmark/warning) to reassure user input is valid.

top_3_priorities: Extract state orchestration from ProgressiveFlow into custom hook + reducer to reduce 2670-line mega-component to <1500 lines, improve predictability and testability of state transitions

Create unified decision-point UI for choosing progressive vs legacy flow at onboarding + add visible affordances (version history button, persona pool preview) throughout the voyage to surface powerful features users miss

Redesign mobile layout from fixed padding workarounds to true responsive architecture with container queries, SafeArea context, and breakpoint-aware rail visibility so small screens feel native, not squeezed

audits.summary: Argus's visual design successfully implements the stated "dawn harbor" (Ì≥´Î£ûÌ≥≠Ì≤ãÌ≤Ä Ì≥´ÎÄ°Ì≥¨ÏìΩ Ì≥≠ÎπÜÊè¥Ì≤¨) philosophy with strong color tokens, premium typography, and intentional motion design. However, the implementation shows gaps between the high-minded design intent and the actual product experience: spacing is inconsistent at small scales, component hierarchy lacks visual distinction, some workspace interactions feel generic rather than "editorial," and dark mode colors drift from the philosophy. The landing page excels at the voyage metaphor, but the product workspace defaults to functional clarity over warmth and generosity of space. Overall, the design is competent and accessible, but misses the premium, calm, editorial feel that the philosophy promises.

audits.area: OUTPUT ARTIFACTS Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î Ithaca (Project Brief / Prompt Chain / Agent Spec / Execution Checklist)
audits.summary: Argus generates 5 types of markdown/YAML artifacts (Project Brief, Prompt Chain, Agent Spec, Decision Rationale, Execution Checklist) from structured voyage data. These are currently static document generators (1200 LoC total) with zero persistence, zero integration, and zero feedback loops. Phase 5 roadmap (Output Revolution) promises "context-aware, assumption-validating, live artifacts" but artifacts today are intentionally stateless and disconnected from execution. No mechanism exists to track if a downloaded Agent Spec was actually implemented, if checklist steps were executed, or if real-world execution validated the assumptions that shaped the artifact. The system produces beautiful "thought trail" documents (Thought Trajectory, Rationale) but delivers no execution bridge.

audits.summary: ARGUS is a sophisticated decision harness with mature Phase 1-2 implementation (1004 passing tests, clean build, 144 eslint warnings mostly unused vars). The core LLM layer (src/lib/llm.ts, 789 lines) is robust with proper error categorization and multi-fallback JSON parsing. However, the codebase exhibits moderate-to-high architectural debt: ProgressiveFlow.tsx is 2670 lines monolithic component, useProgressiveStore.ts is 1786 lines with mixed responsibilities, store coupling is undisciplined (19 stores with overlapping state domains), and critical test coverage gaps exist for 60+ untested lib modules (agent-*, orchestrator-*, worker-*). Type-safety holes include 267 instances of type casts (as any/unknown), unvalidated LLM output consumption in 55+ JSON.parse calls, and per-CLAUDE.md, duplicated FEEDBACK_SYSTEM prompts creating sync risks. The 144 eslint warnings break down as: ~45 unused imports (easy fixes), ~25 unused variables (dead code), ~15 missing hook dependencies (correctness risks), ~50 diverse issues.

research.topic: ARGUS Design Audit: Premium Editorial Standards & Visual Debt Assessment
key_insights: ProgressiveFlow.tsx is 2670 lines Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î monolithic state machine that conflates orchestration with presentation. Blocks extraction of small, reusable design tokens and motion patterns. Makes it impossible to apply consistent polish at component boundaries.

Color system is sophisticated (warm ivory/navy/gold, risk 3-category, semantic AI/human/collab zones) but scattered usage: backdrop-blur-xl on Header/Sidebar violates 'editorial, not tech' aesthetic; bg-blue-50, bg-purple-100 hardcoded in legacy components (FeedbackRequest, PersonaCard, FeedbackResult) breaks palette harmony.

Motion is unrefined: active:scale[0.97] and hover:-translate-y[1px] feels mechanical (bouncy/jittery) Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î conflicts with stated design mood 'slow elegant motion cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)'. Duration-200ms global default is too brisk for premium editorial feel. No page-level entrance rhythm.

Typography system exists (serif display + sans body + mono code) but underutilized: workspace components use inline style={{ fontFamily }} instead of consistent semantic classes. Landing uses font-display correctly; workspace reverted to ad-hoc approach. No vertical rhythm enforcement (line-height not scaled per size).

Spacing inconsistency: tailwind gap-* scattered (gap-2, gap-8, gap-3, gap-1.5 in single component). No design token adoption. globals.css defines --radius-sm through --radius-2xl but components use tailwind rounded-xl/rounded-12px. No 8px/16px/24px/32px ladder.

Blue/purple accent colors (used for intensity signals) violate warm palette Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î these should map to gold gradient or be replaced with warm grays. Risk critical/manageable/unspoken use correct warm palette (#E24B4A, #EF9F27, #7F77DD) but secondary UI (button states, focus rings, feedback urgency) reverted to standard Tailwind primaries.

Blueprint system (landing-scoped, Ïß†6.2 in globals.css) is beautiful but isolated Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î 1px/1.5px hairline rules, monospaced labels, aged-parchment paper, navy ink never appear in workspace. Workspace uses flat white surfaces instead. Creates two-tier aesthetic.

Accessibility baseline met (106 aria/role/alt attributes) but spacing between focus rings and content sometimes inadequate. alt text missing on decorative emojis (no harm but inconsistent). 14px text in dense lists too small for extended reading at comfortable arm's distance.

Button component has accent variant (gradient-gold) but most CTAs use primary (solid dark). No visual hierarchy signal Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î important actions (generate, review) same weight as dismissals. Danger variant hardcoded red-50 instead of matching warm palette.

Responsive design works (media queries at 480px/640px) but lacks tablet optimization. Gap from mobile layout (16px padding) to desktop (24-56px) is jarring. No container queries for adaptive components Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î ProgressiveFlow card widths not optimized for 768-1024px viewports.

Loading states use generic skeleton + placeholder-exit animations. No phase-specific 'ambient glow' for analytical phases (PhaseAmbient exists but relies on radial-gradient, not refined). Smooth waits are key editorial touchstone Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î current implementation is functional but not memorable.

Output artifacts (4-item Ithaca, FinalCard) generated as static markdown Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î no design-aware rendering. Serif typography not applied to output previews. Callouts/blockquotes rendered with generic styles, not editorial serif hierarchy.
concrete_patterns: Extract a `useDesignSystem` hook that centralizes all design tokens (colors, spacing, radius, easing, shadows, typography families) and exposes them as CSS custom properties to all components. Eliminates scattered hardcoded values. Start: `src/hooks/useDesignSystem.ts` Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î returns { colors, spacing, radius, ease, shadow, typography } objects mapped to CSS vars.

Establish motion grammar: Page entrance (stagger by 100ms), section scroll (fade-up 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)), state change (180ms), micro-interaction (120ms). Document in `src/styles/motion.config.ts`. Apply via Framer Motion presets, not inline transitions. Replace duration-200 global with duration-150 (form input) / 200 (card) / 300 (page transition).

Normalize spacing to 8px ladder: gap-1=4px, gap-2=8px, gap-3=12px, gap-4=16px, gap-6=24px, gap-8=32px, gap-12=48px. Apply via Tailwind theme overrides, not magic numbers. Enforce with ESLint rule `no-arbitrary-values: ['gap', 'px', 'py', 'mb', 'mt', 'px']` Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î forces designers to use tokens.

Refactor Button component: Remove hardcoded red-50/red-200 for danger. Use semantic danger variant that maps to warm-palette-derived (e.g., #C85A4A with #EDD3CD background). Add priority levels: primary (gold gradient), secondary (dark text + border), tertiary (text only + underline), danger (warm-red). Always use CSS vars, never hardcoded colors.

Create editorial typography system: Define three scales (content: 14px base + 1.7 line-height; heading: serif clamp(20px, 3vw, 28px) bold -0.01em letter-spacing; label: 11px uppercase 0.12em tracking). Apply via `@apply` classes (.text-content, .text-heading-md, .text-label) to enforce vertical rhythm. Workspace components must use classes, not inline style={{ fontFamily }}.

Extract ProgressiveFlow into 5 domain components: (1) PhaseOrchestrator (state machine only), (2) PhaseRenderer (maps phaseÌ≥¢ÎÑÇcomponent), (3) ProgressBar (visual stepper + phase labels), (4) ErrorBoundary (LLM error states), (5) OutputSequence (4-item ithaca assembly). Each <500 lines, testable, reusable design tokens per component.

Unify Header/Sidebar: Replace backdrop-blur-xl with subtle warm vignette (--gradient-warm-vignette). Maintain 'editorial' feel: solid surface with hairline border, not glassmorphic. Apply navigation links with semantic hover (scale 1.02, gold underline, no color flash). Keep z-index sticky but remove the 'floating' illusion.

Establish color contrast compliance: All text must be WCAG AA (4.5:1 minimum). Audit: primary text on --bg (Ì≥¢ÏêØ 10:1), secondary on surface (Ì≥¢ÏêØ 6.5:1), tertiary on surface (Ì≥¢Ïêµ 3.2:1 Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î too light). Replace --text-tertiary (#b0aa9f) with #8b8174 for minimum 5:1. Use WebAIM contrast checker to validate all combinations.

Blueprint (landing) Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ Workspace bridge: Adopt blueprint grid (24px dot matrix at ~6% opacity) as optional page backdrop in Workspace intro / empty states. Introduce blueprint hairlines (1px var(--bp-ink-faint)) to workspace cards. Use blueprint-scoped button styles (squared, monospaced label) in export dialogs + system controls (only, not every CTA).

Load animation refinement: Replace generic skeleton with 'drift' effect Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î animated wave across surface (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), 2s duration). Add phase-aware messaging: 'Ì≥≠ÎπÜÊø°ÏíïÌ≤•Ì≤º Ê¥πÎ™É‚îÅÊÄ®Ì≤† Ì≥¨Ïó≥Ì≥¨ÎíøÌ≥´Îï≤Ì≥´Îñé' (Redraw interval: 0.5s, subtle scale pulse). No loading spinners Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î use text + motion only.

Typography scale enforcement: Use Tailwind v4 fluid typography plugins (`clamp()`) for responsive heading sizing. Example: .text-display-lg uses clamp(24px, 3.5vw, 40px), never hardcoded 28px. Extend theme with named sizes (display-xl, display-lg, display-md, heading, subheading, body, caption, mono-code) Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î component authors pick semantic name, not pixel value.

Risk color integration: Audit all UI signaling. Replace scattered blue-50/red-100/purple-100 with gradient backgrounds derived from --risk-* tokens. Example: critical risk callout uses linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(226,75,74,0.06) 0%, rgba(226,75,74,0.02) 100%) + border rgba(226,75,74,0.25). Maintain warm palette harmony across all feedback surfaces.

Accessibility audit & enforcement: Add axe-core automated testing to CI/CD. Set rules: color contrast minimum 4.5:1 (text), 3:1 (components), touch targets Ì≥¢Îèü44x44px. Disable focus ring outline on decorative buttons. Use explicit ARIA labels on all icon buttons. Document in ACCESSIBILITY.md Ì≥¢Ì≤ÄÌ≤î e.g., 'All feedback badges must pass axe contrast check before merge'.

Container queries for workspace cards: Replace fixed max-w-[480px] with @container (min-width: 480px) queries. Allows cards to reflow from single-column (mobile) Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ two-column (tablet) Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ detail-expanded (desktop) without media-query breakpoints. Start: FinalCard, AnalysisCard, WorkflowGraph.

Output artifact rendering overhaul: Create `src/lib/editorial-renderer.ts` that renders 4 Ithaca outputs with applied typography + spacing semantics. Markdown headings rendered with serif font-display, proper vertical rhythm, gold accent underlines. Blockquotes italicized + left border (1.5px var(--accent)). Code blocks use --font-mono with subtle background var(--bg).

research.topic: Production Resilience Patterns for Streaming LLM Web Apps: Argus Audit & Industry Best Practices (2025-2026)
key_insights: Argus has strong foundational error handling (categorized LLMError with retryable flags, circuit breaker per provider) but lacks end-to-end timeout + cancellation strategy for streaming responses, creating risk of hung requests. Streaming SSE parser handles malformed chunks gracefully (line 728 in llm.ts) but doesn't implement request-level timeouts or partial-result recovery.

Worker engine (worker-engine.ts) executes in parallel with concurrency limits but doesn't distinguish between transient + permanent failures during streaming. Validation failures trigger automatic retry (line 259-273) but there's no budget/backoff; could retry forever if validation always fails.

ProgressiveFlow (2670 lines) renders error state correctly (lines 2452, 2634) with dismiss/retry UX but doesn't implement skeleton/partial-render patterns used by Claude.ai/ChatGPT. On network failure mid-stream, user sees blank card until full restart.

No offline-first pattern: localStorage stores decompose/recast/persona data but real-time streaming results (the output users see) aren't cached. If connection drops mid-stream, progress is lost. Supabase sync is async but doesn't pre-emptively store partial results.

JSON parse retry (callLLMStreamThenParse lines 765-789) attempts 3 strategies (code fences Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ outermost object Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ array) but doesn't implement the 'truncated JSON recovery' pattern: keeping partial-but-valid JSON when stream cuts off mid-chunk (common at 2k-4k token boundaries).

No request timeout at fetch() level. AbortController is passed through (line 20, 144, 249) but no explicit timer. A hung provider could block indefinitely. Industry standard: 30-90s timeout for streaming requests.

Rate limit handling (lines 69-76) distinguishes anonymous-quota-exhausted from provider-throttle but doesn't implement the exponential backoff + jitter pattern comprehensively. Header-based retry_after is parsed but only stored locally (lines 73, 186); not propagated to UI for user-facing countdown.

Graceful degradation missing: no fallback to cached previous results, no 'continue from checkpoint' pattern, no 'use cheaper model' strategy. If Anthropic 429s, there's no fallback to OpenAI/Gemini that's configured.

Streaming UX gap: on error mid-stream, worker callbacks (onError at line 288) set a string message. UI shows alert but doesn't show 'what we got so far' + regenerate button. Leading products show partial synthesis + 'Continue' button.
concrete_patterns: TIMEOUT STRATEGY: Add AbortController-based timeout at callLLMStream() entry. Recommended: 60s for normal tasks, 120s for max-tokens=4000 contexts. Pattern: const controller = new AbortController(); const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 60000); merge with user signal: const mergedSignal = ...; Implement in llm.ts lines 627-680 BEFORE fetch().

PARTIAL RESULT RECOVERY: Modify callLLMStreamThenParse (lines 765-789) to emit partial-JSON checkpoints. After each onToken, attempt parseJSON on fullText; if valid, snapshot to sessionStorage. On parse error at completion, return last-valid checkpoint instead of failing. Pattern: const checkpoints = []; onToken: if (valid JSON detected) checkpoints.push({text, timestamp}); onError: if (checkpoints.length > 0) resolve(checkpoints[checkpoints.length - 1]).

STREAMING SKELETON UI: In ProgressiveFlow.tsx, add phase-aware skeleton while streaming. On worker.onStart, render <div className='animate-pulse' /> with height matching expected output. On token, gradually replace skeleton. On error, keep skeleton visible + show partial result + 'Regenerate' button. Reference: Framer Motion skeleton patterns in AnalysisCard.tsx (~shared/AnalysisCard).

OFFLINE-FIRST PARTIAL RESULTS: Extend Zustand stores (useProgressiveStore) to pre-emptively write streaming text chunks to localStorage every 500ms during onToken. On mount, check localStorage for partial session state. Pattern: const savePartial = debounce((text) => localStorage.setItem('session_' + sessionId + '_partial', text), 500); Pass to all onToken callbacks.

RETRY BUDGET + EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF: Add RetryPolicy interface to worker-engine.ts. Pattern: { maxRetries: 2, baseDelayMs: 1000, maxDelayMs: 30000, jitterFraction: 0.25 }. Replace lines 199-200 (hardcoded MAX_RETRIES=1) with dynamic retry logic: nextDelay = Math.min(baseDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt), maxDelayMs) * (1 + jitterFraction * (Math.random() - 0.5)).

GRACEFUL MODEL DEGRADATION: In callLLM (lines 377-403), if Anthropic returns 429 or 503, check if user has OpenAI/Gemini keys configured. Pattern: try anthropic; catch (429/503) => if (settings.openai_api_key) fallback to OpenAI; Update error.retryable flag to false after fallback to prevent infinite retry.

CIRCUIT BREAKER ENHANCEMENT: Current circuit (lines 104-149) uses simple count + reset. Add sliding-window to detect transient vs sustained failures. Pattern: track failures in 60s window, not lifetime count. If 5 failures in 60s, open for 30s. If 2+ failures per second, open circuit + skip to fallback provider.

STREAMING ERROR RECOVERY UI: In ProgressiveFlow worker callbacks (lines 204-210), add recovery action. Pattern: onError callback should include: { error, partialText, canRetry, fallbackText }. If partialText exists, show AnalysisCard with partial content + red border. Add 'Regenerate' + 'Use this (unverified)' buttons. Reference: ErrorState pattern in DMFeedback.tsx.

REQUEST TIMEOUT + VISIBLE COUNTDOWN: Add visual timeout indicator in worker UI. Pattern: const [secondsRemaining, setSecondsRemaining] = useState(60); useEffect(() => { const interval = setInterval(() => setSecondsRemaining(s => s - 1), 1000); return () => clearInterval(interval); }, []); Render subtle timer in loading state. At 10s remaining, switch to amber color. At 0, show 'Request timed out. Retrying...'

JSON TRUNCATION RECOVERY: Replace parseJSON multi-fallback (lines 221-264) with truncation-aware strategy. Pattern: if parseJSON fails and fullText.length > 3500, try: (1) remove last incomplete line + parse; (2) find last complete } at depth 0 + parse that object; (3) treat as cancelled/partial, return { _partial: true, text: fullText }. Update consumers to handle _partial flag.

RATE LIMIT DISPLAY + COUNTDOWN: Expose rate-limit state in Zustand store. On CustomEvent 'argus:ratelimit' (line 722), update store. In ProgressiveFlow header, add small badge: 'Uses: 3/10 today Ï®å resets in 4h'. If approaching limit, show warning toast. Pattern: useRateLimitStore() with countdown timer updating every 60s.

PROVIDER-LEVEL ERROR CONTEXT: Extend LLMError to include provider + endpoint. Update error display (error-display.ts lines 15-95) to show: 'Anthropic API is experiencing issues (503). Retrying with OpenAI...' instead of generic 'Server error'. Pattern: pass provider to categorizeError; include in error.message.

CHECKPOINT-BASED RESUME: For long-running synthesis (recast, rehearsal), emit checkpoint after each section. Store checkpoints in Supabase drafts table. If interrupted, show 'Resume from checkpoint 2/5' button. Pattern: buildCheckpoint(section, text, metadata) Ì≥¢ÎÑÇ upsert to drafts; onResume, fetch latest checkpoint + append new tokens.

SSE PARSER ROBUSTNESS: Current parser (lines 700-745) handles incomplete lines but doesn't detect/recover from connection interruption during chunk. Pattern: detect if 2+ seconds pass without data, emit 'connection_stalled' event. UI shows 'Connection slow. Waiting...' At 5s, trigger automatic reconnect with session ID to resume from last token offset.

WORKER VALIDATION BYPASS: Worker validation (worker-quality.ts) can fail due to LLM-side errors (e.g., Claude returns null for some fields). Instead of retry loop (line 259-273), add 'Accept unvalidated' path. Pattern: if validation fails after 1 retry, set validation.score = 50, validation.passed = false, but include flag validation.incomplete = true. Show UI: 'Quality check incomplete. Use anyway?' + warning badge.

The plan's R7 mentions 'rollback' but frames it as a modal-state cleanup, not as the philosophy-violating default.
